Videos are made on Kaggle’s free GPU, not on this website. We pack your settings into a Kaggle notebook, so you never edit code. Your image, if you added one, goes inside the notebook too.

    Open Kaggle ↗

    Before you start on Kaggle

    You need a free Kaggle account with a verified phone number (Kaggle requires it to turn on GPUs and internet). No card is ever needed. Kaggle gives about 30 free GPU hours a week, and a GPU isn’t always free straight away, so a run may wait in a queue.

    Run it on
    Kaggle.

    This page can’t see inside Kaggle, so it won’t show progress it doesn’t have. Kaggle’s Versions list shows the real status of your run.

    1. Import the notebook

      Do: on Kaggle, tap Create → New Notebook, then File → Import Notebook, and pick the file you just downloaded.

      You’ll see: a notebook titled “BLVCKDISK AI Studio — one real video”.

      On a phone: use your browser’s “Desktop site” option if menus are missing.

    2. Turn on the free GPU and internet

      Do: open the right-hand panel (the ‹ tab on the edge) → Session options → Accelerator GPU T4 x2, Internet On.

      Why: the model needs a GPU to run and the internet to download its files (about 17 GB, a few minutes).

    3. Start the run in the background

      Do: Save Version → Save & Run All (Commit) → Save.

      Why: this runs on Kaggle’s servers. You can lock your phone or close the tab.

      Tip: afterwards, tap the power icon at the top to close the editor so it doesn’t use your GPU hours.

    4. Wait for the green check

      Do: open your notebook’s Versions list now and then. “Queued” means waiting for a free GPU; “Running” means it’s working; a check mark means it’s done.

      Typical time: our reference run (2 seconds, draft size) generated in 204 seconds, plus about 5–10 minutes of setup. Bigger settings take longer.

    5. Download your video

      Do: open the finished version → Output → first_video.mp4 → download.

      Next: come back here and import it. Kaggle files disappear when the session is gone, so keep the download.

    Something went wrong?

    “NO GPU” or it’s very slow

    The GPU wasn’t on. Session options → Accelerator → GPU T4 x2, then Save & Run All again.

    Internet switch is greyed out

    Kaggle needs a verified phone number first: profile → Settings → Phone verification. Then turn Internet On.

    Model download failed

    Usually a brief network hiccup. Save & Run All again; already-finished steps simply repeat.

    Stuck on “Queued” for a long time

    All free GPUs are busy, or another session of yours holds one. Close any open Kaggle editors (power icon). If it stays queued, cancel the run and start it again, or pick GPU P100 instead.

    “Out of memory” error

    The settings were too big for the free GPU. Go back, choose Draft size or a shorter length, and prepare a new notebook.

    “Generation failed” or a red error

    Run it once more. If it fails again, prepare a new notebook with Draft size and Fast quality. The red text explains the cause.

    No first_video.mp4 in Output

    The run didn’t finish. Open the version’s log and scroll to the red text. Sessions also end after 12 hours, or if the run was stopped.
